correctness.rationale: The two-marker period restriction and maximal extension formula are proved directly; the sharp maximum follows by splitting p <= floor((n+1)/3) and p greater, with exact equality cases. A uniform lattice-simplex limit yields a two-atom law and an explicit density after exact area integration. Direct interval enumeration agrees for all 2600 cases of lengths 2..25 and 873 seeded cases, with finite tests supplementary.

value.rationale: The exact maximum, rigid extremizer census, and limit with two atoms and density 6/(2+y)^3 give a motivated complete law for the fundamental maximal-repetition exponent-sum invariant in a natural sparse class. The limiting mean is zero after centering despite a nonzero limiting variance, a substantive phenomenon not explained by global bounds.
